sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: The sticky first column's set-up now does all its style changes before reading any cell's colour back, instead of alternating cell by cell. The colours it stores, and the row hover, are unchanged; the time saved is small now that the collapse set-up no longer forces layout (PERFORMANCE.org Step 41).

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Tests: tests/fixtures/sticky-column-batched.spec.js (one read group; stored colours equal what the cells paint; hover paints and restores) through the new __saTest.sticky.apply hook; 2 more mutations, caught.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Redrawing a large table after a filter is quicker on pages with several collapsible columns: the multi-row/prose collapse set-up now measures all columns in one go instead of one column at a time, each of which made the browser lay out the whole table again. On a 4,174-row events page that part fell by three quarters (PERFORMANCE.org Step 40).

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Tests: tests/fixtures/collapse-measure-batched.spec.js (reads in at most two groups, same outcome) through the new __saTest.collapse.init hook; one more mutation, caught. tests/support/probe-keystroke-cost.js gains --cpu (a V8 CPU profile of one typed run, inclusive time per function).

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Typing a filter on a table of more than 1,000 rows freezes the page far less. The filter now compares rows a few milliseconds at a time and lets the page respond in between; a key typed while a filter runs replaces it, and the replaced filter changes nothing. Measured: the slowest key typed during a filter fell from 1.6-1.9 s to 0.1-0.5 s on single-table pages, and from about 0.9 s to 0.6 s on a 47-table page, where drawing the result is still one step (PERFORMANCE.org Step 39).

The ⏳ Sorting and filtering card now shows a long filter while it runs: what you are filtering for, the rows compared so far and how many match; afterwards the comparing and drawing times; its Recent list notes a filter replaced by a newer one.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Tests: tests/fixtures/filter-sliced.spec.js (9) and its mobile twin: same rows, order, status and highlights as a synchronous pass on single- and multi-table pages; column-filter typing sliced too; a pass replaced by a newer key, the ✕ clear or a sort writes nothing; _renderSettled held while comparing; the card's states and log. Driven through the new __saTest.filterSlicing hooks. 13 more mutations in scripts/mutations/faster-filtering.json: 11 caught, 2 recorded as expect pass with the reason.

Help: the progress card section now describes live filter progress. Docs: filter-and-cache-invariants.md (a sliced pass writes nothing until current and complete), toolbar-and-header-ui.md (the tablework provider), performance-rules.md (the typed metric and the keystroke probe).

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Typing right after a large table renders is no longer slowed by the column-header counts filling in. The counts are now written in batches, at most every half second and once at the end, instead of column by column; each write made the next keystroke lay out the whole table again, 74-163 ms each on a 4,174-row page (PERFORMANCE.org Step 38). A count scan replaced by a newer one no longer leaves a partial set of numbers behind.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Tests: tests/fixtures/header-counts-batched.spec.js (one task writes every badge, against a per-column control; a scan superseded mid-way publishes nothing), driven through the new __saTest.colHeaderCounts hooks; 3 more mutations in scripts/mutations/faster-filtering.json, all caught. uniq-drop-count-click-toggle.spec.js now waits for the count badge to have its number before clicking it.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Typing in a filter box on a large table no longer repaints the whole visible table on every key. Every data table now has its own paint layer, so one character costs about 18 ms of painting instead of about 75 ms on a 4,174-row page (PERFORMANCE.org Step 37).

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Tests: tests/fixtures/table-paint-layer.spec.js (single- and multi-table, sticky headers off, the stuck header still covering scrolled rows) and its mobile twin; scripts/mutations/faster-filtering.json (5 planted defects, all caught). All 64 sticky-header specs pass with the new stacking context.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Measuring typed filtering. capture-interaction-perf.js --only=typed types each filter value one key at a time with a pause (--typing-delays=150,400) and records, per key and per sample, the slowest keystroke (Event Timing), the longest animation frame and task, the wait after the last key and the number of filter passes. Earlier filter numbers were single-pass; this is the first measure of a person typing. Its files carry a -typed suffix, and scripts/run-perf-arms.py keeps a separate ETA history for such runs.

Baselines for main (9.99.1316) on artist-events, artist-releases-dylan, artist-releasegroups and artist-recordings-petty, run twice in opposite orders (tests/MEASUREMENTS.org, "Typed filtering"; table from the new scripts/summarize-typed-perf.py). With a pause longer than the debounce, a keystroke waits 0.85-1.9 s and the page goes up to 1.96 s without painting.

New probe tests/support/probe-keystroke-cost.js: traces typing right after the render and once the header counts have settled, and lists every slow main-thread task with what ran in it; --css= and --init= test a remedy without changing the userscript. It found two costs outside runFilter(): each key repaints the whole visible table (about 75 ms; a paint layer on the table cuts it to about 18 ms), and right after the render each header-count badge write makes the next key re-lay out the whole table (DEBUG-NOTES.md, 2026-10-10).
